A monolith is an application built and deployed as one unit, its parts in one process; a modular monolith keeps that deployment but splits code into modules, each owning one bounded context's model and data, reachable only through a small public part.

Being a monolith is a deployment choice, not a design flaw; modules address parts reaching freely into each other's data; split services reading the same tables are still tangled; with its own database, notifications' email row cannot join the order's SaveChangesAsync.
Method calls and one transaction over several tables, which one process and one database give, are worth keeping while the parts have no reason to be deployed separately.
